newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Orion Capital sees Q4 EPS $1.35-37.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Orion Capital sees Q4 EPS $1.35-37.

text.p: Orion Capital Corp expects to report fourth quarter operating earnings in the range of $1.35-$1.37 a share, ahead of Wall Street's expectations, the company's chief executive Marston Becker said.
Analysts had a fourth quarter consensus estimate of $1.31 a share for Orion Capital, according to First Call.
For the full year, Orion Capital expects to report operating earnings in the range of $5.22-$5.25 a share, Becker told Reuters in a telephone interview.
That compares with the First Call consensus of $5.12 a share.
Becker said he expects fourth quarter net premiums written to rise about 85 percent to $338 million and total revenue to rise 67 percent to $398 million.

Orion Capital expects to report a fourth quarter combined ratio of 99.6 percent compared with 100.1 percent a year ago, Becker said, and the 1996 combined ratio is expected to fall below 100 percent for the first time ever for a full accounting year, he said.
Net income for the full year is expected to rise 25-30 percent over 1995, he said.
Revenues for 1996 are expected to rise about 70 percent to almost $1.5 billion, with much of that coming from Orion's increased stake in Guaranty National Corp.
Orion Capital this year raised its stake in Guaranty National to about 80 percent from 49.5 percent.
Becker said the fourth quarter and full year earnings got a boost from improved performances in all its businesses.
"Even with the price competition, we are continuing to see good organic growth in our businesses," he said.
"We really feel that the positioning of each of our businesses has been driving our performance."
The EBI Cos workers compensation business saw organic growth in its revenues and achieved a combined ratio that was nine to 10 points better than the industry average, Becker said.
The combined ratio indicates whether or not a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
The DPIC professional liability business grew despite an extremely tough environment, Becker said.
And Guaranty National also was a contributor to earnings, he said.
He said Orion Capital plans to boost its participation in the Wm. H. McGee & Co, a manager of marine insurance underwriting pools, to 50 percent in 1997 from 37 percent in 1996.
Meanwhile, a repositioning of business at Connecticut Specialty Insurance Group has resulted in a sharp, six to seven point drop in the combined ratio to better than industry average, Becker said.
Becker expects the company to achieve return on equity of 14 percent in 1996.
"We continue to feel our outlook for the future remains bright," he said.
-- Patricia Vowinkel 212-859-1716
